title: Pre-Calculus — Mathematics and the Mind of God: Unit Quiz

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function?
questions.explanation: A circle fails the Vertical Line Test — for most x-values, there are two corresponding y-values. A function requires exactly one output for each input.

questions.question: What is the domain of f(x) = 1/(x - 3)?
questions.explanation: The function is undefined when the denominator equals zero: x - 3 = 0, so x = 3 is excluded from the domain.

questions.question: A polynomial of degree 4 has at most how many turning points?
questions.explanation: A polynomial of degree n has at most n - 1 turning points. A degree 4 polynomial has at most 3 turning points.

questions.question: What is log₂(32)?
questions.explanation: log₂(32) asks: '2 to what power equals 32?' Since 2⁵ = 32, log₂(32) = 5.

questions.question: Using the compound interest formula A = P(1 + r)ᵗ, if you invest $1,000 at 10% annual interest for 3 years, how much will you have?
questions.explanation: A = 1000(1 + 0.10)³ = 1000(1.1)³ = 1000(1.331) = $1,331.00. Compound interest grows the investment by 10% each year, applied to the new total.

questions.question: On the unit circle, what are the coordinates of the point at angle π/4 (45°)?
questions.explanation: At π/4 (45°), both sine and cosine equal √2/2, so the coordinates are (cos 45°, sin 45°) = (√2/2, √2/2).

questions.question: What is the sum of the arithmetic series 2 + 5 + 8 + 11 + 14?
questions.explanation: This arithmetic series has 5 terms with a₁ = 2 and a₅ = 14. S₅ = 5/2 × (2 + 14) = 5/2 × 16 = 40.

questions.question: What is the sum of the infinite geometric series 1 + 1/3 + 1/9 + 1/27 + ...?
questions.explanation: This is an infinite geometric series with a₁ = 1 and r = 1/3. Since |r| < 1, S = a₁/(1-r) = 1/(1 - 1/3) = 1/(2/3) = 3/2.

questions.question: What is lim(x→2) (x² - 4)/(x - 2)?
questions.explanation: Factor the numerator: (x² - 4)/(x - 2) = (x+2)(x-2)/(x-2) = x + 2 for x ≠ 2. As x → 2, x + 2 → 4.

questions.question: The Fibonacci sequence appears in flower petals, seed spirals, and branching patterns. Many Christian mathematicians see this as evidence of:
options: Intelligent design by a Creator who embedded mathematical beauty in nature
Human projection of patterns onto nature
questions.explanation: The consistent appearance of the Fibonacci sequence across diverse living things points to a Designer who embedded mathematical order and beauty into the structure of creation, reflecting His wisdom (Romans 1:20).
